pr_title: Fixes LineEdit emitting text_change with max chars
pr_body:
When LineEdit reached the maximum characters, it stopped appending text but would still emit `LineEdit::_text_changed()`.

This PR also resolves the issue of `LineEdit::_text_changed()` not being emitted on certain situations when `LineEdit::append_at_cursor()` is called but no `LineEdit::_text_changed()` is called afterwards (e.g. LineEdit::set_text()).

Also adds a new signal: "text_change_rejected" which is emitted when trying to add text to the field is unsuccessful due to reaching the maximum character limit.

Closes: #33318
pr_comments: BTW about #33318 (*Edit:* Fixed issue number), I wonder if it's a bug or an expected behavior. If you don't get any signal when LineEdit discards your input, you're not able to react to it. Maybe there'd be a need for a `text_change_failed` signal of some sort?
@codecustard Is this still desired? If so, it needs to be rebased on the latest master branch.

issue_context.title: text_changed in LineEdit is emitted even if text doesn't change due to maximum length
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2 alpha3

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Add LineEdit
2. Connect text_changed signal to a method that prints something
3. Add maximum length to the edit
4. Run the project and hold some letter key
5. The signal keeps being emitted

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[ReproductionProject.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3802198/ReproductionProject.zip)
comments:
Started a discussion on #33417, but I'm not sure if it's a bug per se, or if fixing this bug would actually create a missing feature.

Currently you would be able to use the `text_changed` signal in such a situation to find out that the text input was actually discarded (you cache previous text, on text changed you check that the new text is still the same as old text). If we remove the signal, users attempting to input new characters in a full LineEdit will trigger no signal, so you can't handle it in a way that gives them relevant feedback.
How about a new signal for text overflow?
Agreed, a new signal along the lines of `text_change_rejected` would be ideal, rather then providing no feedback.

review_comments: I'm not sure about this, it seems to defeat the purpose of the surrounding `text_changed_dirty` logic here.

I'm not entirely sure about `text_changed_dirty`

> BTW about #33417, I wonder if it's a bug or an expected behavior. If you don't get any signal when LineEdit discards your input, you're not able to react to it. Maybe there'd be a need for a `text_change_failed` signal of some sort?

That's true, it actually makes sense that you'd want some sort of signal.
